newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran firm likely winner in Soroush bid.
newsitem.headline: Iran firm likely winner in Soroush bid.

text.p: A state-owned Iranian engineering firm is emerging as the most likely winner of a deal to develop an Iranian offshore field, Iranian industry sources said on Monday.

Iranian Offshore Engineering Construction Company (IOEC) is confident it is on track to sign a contract for the Soroush oilfield which will lift Iranian oil output by 60,000 barrels per day after a four-year redevelopment costing $245 million.

"We are meeting with the client (NIOC) on Wednesday and we are confident we have the contract," said Nozar Arian, director of business development at IOEC, which is headed by Mehdi Hashemi Rafsanjani, son of Iran's president.

The company's position in the bidding for Soroush had been strengthened by securing two loan packages totalling $160 million from the commodity trade finance group at Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank.
A senior NIOC official in charge of the project would not confirm if IOEC would be granted the contract, citing a confidentiality clause in negotiations.
He said contracts for Soroush and the Balal offshore field would be awarded before the end of March.

Soroush was one of 11 oil and gas projects offered to foreign investors in 1995 which at $6 billion represented the biggest foreign investment opportunity in the Islamic republic since its 1979 revolution.
Successful foreign bidders could fall foul of the U.S. Iran-Libya Sanctions Act which aims to deter foreign investment in Iranian energy.

France's Total SA and Malaysia's state-owned Petroliam Nasional (Petronas) are to date the only direct foreign presence in offshore work under a contract to develop the Sirri E and A oil and gas fields.
European and Asian companies have been in negotiations to develop Soroush and other oil projects in Iran.

The first phase $80 million development of Soroush would see output of 25-35,000 bpd with initial production onstream in two years. A second $165 million phase would see total output of 60,000 bpd in 2000-2001.
IOEC is 51 percent owned by NIOC -- which is responsible for Iran's 2.5 million bpd of crude exports -- and 49 percent by the Industrial Development and Renovation Organisation (IDRO).
